replacements.old: The animals first fixated a stationary target and then tracked a moving target. A wire search coil on one eye measured eye position while an electrode recorded one neuron's spikes.

changes.reason: Identify the two groups, the cells they affect, and position tuning rather than movement direction. Preserve approximate persistence and the following tuning derivation.
changes.source: Main Methods pp. 10-11, Oculomotor integrator network, Eqs. 23-27.

replacements.old: There are two populations, with excitation within each and inhibition between them. Their firing increases for opposite directions of gaze. This supplies the recurrent interaction needed to maintain a range of stored positions.
replacements.new: The model has two groups of integrator neurons. One group fires more when the eye points farther right; the other fires more when it points farther left. Neurons excite cells in their own group and inhibit cells in the other group. The connection strengths are tuned so that the circuit can approximately maintain a range of represented eye positions.

replacements.new: The model scales each spike train into an input $X_i$ with a saturating mean response. A weighted difference between the two groups' synaptic outputs gives the represented eye angle $E_{OI}$. This value sets the firing rates again, closing the feedback loop:
